title: Drinking Water — Specification
scope: This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for drinking water (potable water) supplied through public distribution systems, packaged water sources, borewells, or treated water networks intended for human consumption.
description: IS 10500:2012 is the primary regulatory standard for drinking water in India. It establishes a dual-tier limit system consisting of 'Acceptable Limits' (optimal quality without adverse health effects) and 'Permissible Limits in the Absence of Alternate Source' (upper safety thresholds for difficult terrains). It mandates zero tolerance for microbiological contamination (E. coli and Coliform bacteria) and defines limits for organoleptic, chemical, toxic, and radioactive contaminants.

sections.title: Scope
sections.content: This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for drinking water. It applies to water supplied for human consumption by municipal corporations, panchayats, water utilities, packaged water bottling plants, and individual community water supply schemes.

subsections.title: Applicability
subsections.content: This standard applies to water intended for human consumption, including water used for drinking, cooking, food preparation, and personal hygiene.

sections.title: Normative References
sections.content: The following standards contain provisions which, through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard: IS 1622 (Methods of sampling and microbiological examination of water), IS 3025 (Methods of sampling and physical and chemical examination of water and wastewater in multiple parts), IS 14543 (Packaged drinking water other than packaged natural mineral water).

sections.title: Terminology
sections.content: For the purpose of this standard, drinking water is defined as water intended for human consumption that is clear, free from objectionable taste and odor, pathogenic organisms, toxic chemical substances, and radioactive materials in concentrations that could cause health hazards.

subsections.title: Acceptable Limit
subsections.content: The value of a parameter below which no health hazard is anticipated and water is aesthetically pleasing and wholesome for human consumption.

subsections.title: Permissible Limit in the Absence of Alternate Source
subsections.content: The maximum permissible concentration of a parameter which is acceptable only when no better quality water source is available in the geographic region.

sections.title: Requirements
sections.content: Drinking water shall comply with the organoleptic, physical, chemical, toxicological, and bacteriological requirements prescribed in Tables 1 through 4. Water shall not contain any substance in concentrations exceeding permissible limits.

subsections.title: Organoleptic and Physical Parameters (Table 1)
subsections.content: Color shall not exceed 5 Hazen units (permissible up to 15). Odour shall be agreeable. pH shall range between 6.5 and 8.5 with no relaxation. Taste shall be agreeable. Turbidity shall not exceed 1 NTU (permissible up to 5 NTU). Total Dissolved Solids shall not exceed 500 mg/l (permissible up to 2000 mg/l).

subsections.title: General Chemical Parameters (Table 2)
subsections.content: Total Hardness as CaCO3 shall not exceed 200 mg/l (permissible up to 600 mg/l). Iron content shall not exceed 0.3 mg/l with no relaxation. Chlorides shall not exceed 250 mg/l (permissible up to 1000 mg/l). Fluoride shall not exceed 1.0 mg/l (permissible up to 1.5 mg/l). Nitrate shall not exceed 45 mg/l with no relaxation.

subsections.title: Parameters Concerning Toxic Substances (Table 3)
subsections.content: Toxic contaminants must strictly remain below specified thresholds: Arsenic limit is 0.01 mg/l (0.05 mg/l permissible without alternative source); Cadmium 0.003 mg/l; Total Chromium 0.05 mg/l; Copper 0.05 mg/l (1.5 mg/l permissible); Cyanide 0.05 mg/l; Lead 0.01 mg/l (no relaxation); Mercury 0.001 mg/l (no relaxation); Nickel 0.02 mg/l.

subsections.title: Bacteriological Requirements (Table 4)
subsections.content: All samples of drinking water, whether from piped supplies or community collection points, must show zero detectable count of Escherichia coli (E. coli) or thermotolerant coliform bacteria in any 100 ml sample. Total Coliform bacteria must also not be detectable in any 100 ml sample for treated piped distribution.

sections.title: Sampling and Testing Protocols
sections.content: Representative samples of drinking water shall be drawn in accordance with the procedures prescribed in IS 1622 for microbiological tests and IS 3025 (Part 1) for physical and chemical tests. Testing frequency shall follow municipal guidelines ensuring daily monitoring of chlorine residual and coliforms.
